lovers-complaint-l1: From off a hill whose concave womb reworded
lovers-complaint-l2: A plaintful story from a sistering vale,
lovers-complaint-l3: My spirits to attend this double voice accorded,
lovers-complaint-l4: And down I laid to list the sad-tuned tale;
lovers-complaint-l5: Ere long espied a fickle maid full pale,
lovers-complaint-l6: Tearing of papers, breaking rings a-twain,
lovers-complaint-l7: Storming her world with sorrow’s wind and rain.
lovers-complaint-l8: Upon her head a platted hive of straw,
lovers-complaint-l9: Which fortified her visage from the sun,
lovers-complaint-l10: Whereon the thought might think sometime it saw
lovers-complaint-l11: The carcass of a beauty spent and done:
lovers-complaint-l12: Time had not scythed all that youth begun,
lovers-complaint-l13: Nor youth all quit; but, spite of heaven’s fell rage,
lovers-complaint-l14: Some beauty peep’d through lattice of sear’d age.
lovers-complaint-l15: Oft did she heave her napkin to her eyne,
lovers-complaint-l16: Which on it had conceited characters,
lovers-complaint-l17: Laundering the silken figures in the brine
lovers-complaint-l18: That season’d woe had pelleted in tears,
lovers-complaint-l19: And often reading what contents it bears;
lovers-complaint-l21: In clamours of all size, both high and low.
lovers-complaint-l22: Sometimes her levell’d eyes their carriage ride,
lovers-complaint-l23: As they did battery to the spheres intend;
lovers-complaint-l24: Sometime diverted their poor balls are tied
lovers-complaint-l25: To the orbed earth; sometimes they do extend
lovers-complaint-l26: Their view right on; anon their gazes lend
lovers-complaint-l27: To every place at once, and, nowhere fix’d,
lovers-complaint-l28: The mind and sight distractedly commix’d.
lovers-complaint-l29: Her hair, nor loose nor tied in formal plat,
lovers-complaint-l30: Proclaim’d in her a careless hand of pride;
lovers-complaint-l31: For some, untuck’d, descended her sheaved hat,
lovers-complaint-l32: Hanging her pale and pined cheek beside;
lovers-complaint-l33: Some in her threaden fillet still did bide,
lovers-complaint-l34: And true to bondage would not break from thence,
lovers-complaint-l35: Though slackly braided in loose negligence.
lovers-complaint-l36: A thousand favours from a maund she drew
lovers-complaint-l37: Of amber, crystal, and of beaded jet,
lovers-complaint-l38: Which one by one she in a river threw,
lovers-complaint-l39: Upon whose weeping margent she was set;
lovers-complaint-l40: Like usury, applying wet to wet,
lovers-complaint-l41: Or monarch’s hands that lets not bounty fall
lovers-complaint-l42: Where want cries some, but where excess begs all.
lovers-complaint-l43: Of folded schedules had she many a one,
lovers-complaint-l44: Which she perused, sigh’d, tore, and gave the flood;
lovers-complaint-l45: Crack’d many a ring of posied gold and bone,
lovers-complaint-l46: Bidding them find their sepulchres in mud;
lovers-complaint-l47: Found yet moe letters sadly penn’d in blood,
lovers-complaint-l48: With sleided silk feat and affectedly
lovers-complaint-l49: Enswathed, and seal’d to curious secrecy.
lovers-complaint-l50: These often bathed she in her fluxive eyes,
lovers-complaint-l51: And often kiss’d, and often ’gan to tear;
lovers-complaint-l52: Cried, “O false blood, thou register of lies,
lovers-complaint-l53: What unapproved witness dost thou bear!
lovers-complaint-l54: Ink would have seem’d more black and damned here!”
lovers-complaint-l55: This said, in top of rage the lines she rents,
lovers-complaint-l56: Big discontent so breaking their contents.
lovers-complaint-l57: A reverend man that grazed his cattle nigh⁠—
lovers-complaint-l58: Sometime a blusterer, that the ruffle knew
lovers-complaint-l59: Of court, of city, and had let go by
lovers-complaint-l60: The swiftest hours, observed as they flew⁠—
lovers-complaint-l61: Towards this afflicted fancy fastly drew,
lovers-complaint-l62: And, privileged by age, desires to know
lovers-complaint-l63: In brief the grounds and motives of her woe.
lovers-complaint-l64: So slides he down upon his grained bat,
lovers-complaint-l65: And comely-distant sits he by her side;
lovers-complaint-l66: When he again desires her, being sat,
lovers-complaint-l67: Her grievance with his hearing to divide:
lovers-complaint-l68: If that from him there may be aught applied
lovers-complaint-l69: Which may her suffering ecstasy assuage,
lovers-complaint-l70: ’Tis promised in the charity of age.
lovers-complaint-l71: “Father,” she says, “though in me you behold
lovers-complaint-l72: The injury of many a blasting hour,
lovers-complaint-l73: Let it not tell your judgement I am old;
lovers-complaint-l74: Not age, but sorrow, over me hath power:
lovers-complaint-l75: I might as yet have been a spreading flower,
lovers-complaint-l76: Fresh to myself, if I had self-applied
lovers-complaint-l77: Love to myself and to no love beside.
lovers-complaint-l78: “But, woe is me! too early I attended
lovers-complaint-l79: A youthful suit⁠—it was to gain my grace⁠—
lovers-complaint-l80: Of one by nature’s outwards so commended,
lovers-complaint-l81: That maidens’ eyes stuck over all his face:
lovers-complaint-l82: Love lack’d a dwelling, and made him her place;
lovers-complaint-l83: And when in his fair parts she did abide,
lovers-complaint-l84: She was new lodged and newly deified.
lovers-complaint-l85: “His browny locks did hang in crooked curls;
lovers-complaint-l86: And every light occasion of the wind
lovers-complaint-l87: Upon his lips their silken parcels hurls.
lovers-complaint-l88: What’s sweet to do, to do will aptly find:
lovers-complaint-l89: Each eye that saw him did enchant the mind,
lovers-complaint-l90: For on his visage was in little drawn
lovers-complaint-l91: What largeness thinks in Paradise was sawn.
lovers-complaint-l92: “Small show of man was yet upon his chin;
lovers-complaint-l93: His phoenix down began but to appear
lovers-complaint-l94: Like unshorn velvet on that termless skin
lovers-complaint-l95: Whose bare out-bragg’d the web it seem’d to wear:
lovers-complaint-l96: Yet show’d his visage by that cost more dear;
lovers-complaint-l97: And nice affections wavering stood in doubt
lovers-complaint-l98: If best were as it was, or best without.
lovers-complaint-l99: “His qualities were beauteous as his form,
lovers-complaint-l100: For maiden-tongued he was, and thereof free;
lovers-complaint-l101: Yet if men moved him, was he such a storm
lovers-complaint-l102: As oft ’twixt May and April is to see,
lovers-complaint-l103: When winds breathe sweet, unruly though they be.
lovers-complaint-l104: His rudeness so with his authorized youth
lovers-complaint-l105: Did livery falseness in a pride of truth.
lovers-complaint-l106: “Well could he ride, and often men would say
lovers-complaint-l107: ‘That horse his mettle from his rider takes:
lovers-complaint-l108: Proud of subjection, noble by the sway,
lovers-complaint-l109: What rounds, what bounds, what course, what stop he makes!’
lovers-complaint-l110: And controversy hence a question takes,
lovers-complaint-l111: Whether the horse by him became his deed,
lovers-complaint-l112: Or he his manage by the well-doing steed.
lovers-complaint-l113: “But quickly on this side the verdict went:
lovers-complaint-l114: His real habitude gave life and grace
lovers-complaint-l116: Accomplish’d in himself, not in his case:
lovers-complaint-l117: All aids, themselves made fairer by their place,
lovers-complaint-l118: Came for additions; yet their purposed trim
lovers-complaint-l119: Pieced not his grace, but were all graced by him.
lovers-complaint-l120: “So on the tip of his subduing tongue
lovers-complaint-l121: All kind of arguments and question deep,
lovers-complaint-l122: All replication prompt, and reason strong,
lovers-complaint-l123: For his advantage still did wake and sleep:
lovers-complaint-l124: To make the weeper laugh, the laugher weep,
lovers-complaint-l125: He had the dialect and different skill,
lovers-complaint-l126: Catching all passions in his craft of will:
lovers-complaint-l127: “That he did in the general bosom reign
lovers-complaint-l128: Of young, of old; and sexes both enchanted,
lovers-complaint-l129: To dwell with him in thoughts, or to remain
lovers-complaint-l130: In personal duty, following where he haunted:
lovers-complaint-l131: Consents bewitch’d, ere he desire, have granted;
lovers-complaint-l132: And dialogued for him what he would say,
lovers-complaint-l133: Ask’d their own wills, and made their wills obey.
lovers-complaint-l134: “Many there were that did his picture get,
lovers-complaint-l135: To serve their eyes, and in it put their mind;
lovers-complaint-l136: Like fools that in th’ imagination set
lovers-complaint-l137: The goodly objects which abroad they find
lovers-complaint-l138: Of lands and mansions, theirs in thought assign’d;
lovers-complaint-l139: And labouring in moe pleasures to bestow them
lovers-complaint-l140: Than the true gouty landlord which doth owe them:
lovers-complaint-l141: “So many have, that never touch’d his hand,
lovers-complaint-l142: Sweetly supposed them mistress of his heart.
lovers-complaint-l143: My woeful self, that did in freedom stand,
lovers-complaint-l144: And was my own fee-simple, not in part,
lovers-complaint-l145: What with his art in youth, and youth in art,
lovers-complaint-l146: Threw my affections in his charmed power,
lovers-complaint-l147: Reserved the stalk and gave him all my flower.
lovers-complaint-l148: “Yet did I not, as some my equals did,
lovers-complaint-l149: Demand of him, nor being desired yielded;
lovers-complaint-l150: Finding myself in honour so forbid,
lovers-complaint-l151: With safest distance I mine honour shielded:
lovers-complaint-l152: Experience for me many bulwarks builded
lovers-complaint-l153: Of proofs new-bleeding, which remain’d the foil
lovers-complaint-l154: Of this false jewel, and his amorous spoil.
lovers-complaint-l155: “But, ah, who ever shunn’d by precedent
lovers-complaint-l156: The destined ill she must herself assay?
lovers-complaint-l157: Or forceed examples, ’gainst her own content,
lovers-complaint-l158: To put the by-past perils in her way?
lovers-complaint-l159: Counsel may stop a while what will not stay;
lovers-complaint-l160: For when we rage, advice is often seen
lovers-complaint-l161: By blunting us to make our wits more keen.
lovers-complaint-l162: “Nor gives it satisfaction to our blood,
lovers-complaint-l163: That we must curb it upon others’ proof;
lovers-complaint-l164: To be forbode the sweets that seems so good,
lovers-complaint-l165: For fear of harms that preach in our behoof.
lovers-complaint-l166: O appetite, from judgement stand aloof!
lovers-complaint-l167: The one a palate hath that needs will taste,
lovers-complaint-l168: Though Reason weep, and cry ‘It is thy last.’
lovers-complaint-l169: “For further I could say ‘This man’s untrue,’
lovers-complaint-l170: And knew the patterns of his foul beguiling;
lovers-complaint-l171: Heard where his plants in others’ orchards grew,
lovers-complaint-l172: Saw how deceits were gilded in his smiling;
lovers-complaint-l173: Knew vows were ever brokers to defiling;
lovers-complaint-l174: Thought characters and words merely but art,
lovers-complaint-l175: And bastards of his foul adulterate heart.
lovers-complaint-l176: “And long upon these terms I held my city,
lovers-complaint-l177: Till thus he ’gan besiege me: ‘Gentle maid,
lovers-complaint-l178: Have of my suffering youth some feeling pity,
lovers-complaint-l179: And be not of my holy vows afraid:
lovers-complaint-l180: That’s to ye sworn to none was ever said;
lovers-complaint-l181: For feasts of love I have been call’d unto,
lovers-complaint-l182: Till now did ne’er invite, nor never woo.
lovers-complaint-l183: “ ‘All my offences that abroad you see
lovers-complaint-l184: Are errors of the blood, none of the mind;
lovers-complaint-l185: Love made them not: with acture they may be,
lovers-complaint-l186: Where neither party is nor true nor kind:
lovers-complaint-l187: They sought their shame that so their shame did find;
lovers-complaint-l188: And so much less of shame in me remains,
lovers-complaint-l189: By how much of me their reproach contains.
lovers-complaint-l190: “ ‘Among the many that mine eyes have seen,
lovers-complaint-l191: Not one whose flame my heart so much as warm’d,
lovers-complaint-l192: Or my affection put to the smallest teen,
lovers-complaint-l193: Or any of my leisures ever charm’d:
lovers-complaint-l194: Harm have I done to them, but ne’er was harm’d;
lovers-complaint-l195: Kept hearts in liveries, but mine own was free,
lovers-complaint-l196: And reign’d, commanding in his monarchy.
lovers-complaint-l197: “ ‘Look here, what tributes wounded fancies sent me,
lovers-complaint-l198: Of paled pearls and rubies red as blood;
lovers-complaint-l199: Figuring that they their passions likewise lent me
lovers-complaint-l200: Of grief and blushes, aptly understood
lovers-complaint-l201: In bloodless white and the encrimson’d moods;
lovers-complaint-l202: Effects of terror and dear modesty,
lovers-complaint-l203: Encamp’d in hearts, but fighting outwardly.
lovers-complaint-l204: “ ‘And, lo, behold these talents of their hair,
lovers-complaint-l206: I have received from many a several fair,
lovers-complaint-l208: With the annexions of fair gems enrich’d,
lovers-complaint-l209: And deep-brain’d sonnets that did amplify
lovers-complaint-l210: Each stone’s dear nature, worth, and quality.
lovers-complaint-l212: Whereto his invised properties did tend;
lovers-complaint-l213: The deep-green emerald, in whose fresh regard
lovers-complaint-l214: Weak sights their sickly radiance do amend;
lovers-complaint-l215: The heaven-hued sapphire and the opal blend
lovers-complaint-l216: With objects manifold: each several stone,
lovers-complaint-l217: With wit well blazon’d, smiled or made some moan.
lovers-complaint-l218: “ ‘Lo, all these trophies of affections hot,
lovers-complaint-l219: Of pensived and subdued desires the tender,
lovers-complaint-l220: Nature hath charged me that I hoard them not,
lovers-complaint-l221: But yield them up where I myself must render,
lovers-complaint-l222: That is, to you, my origin and ender;
lovers-complaint-l223: For these, of force, must your oblations be,
lovers-complaint-l224: Since I their altar, you empatron me.
lovers-complaint-l225: “ ‘O, then, advance of yours that phraseless hand,
lovers-complaint-l226: Whose white weighs down the airy scale of praise;
lovers-complaint-l227: Take all these similes to your own command,
lovers-complaint-l228: Hallow’d with sighs that burning lungs did raise;
lovers-complaint-l229: What me your minister, for you obeys,
lovers-complaint-l230: Works under you; and to your audit comes
lovers-complaint-l231: Their distract parcels in combined sums.
lovers-complaint-l232: “ ‘Lo, this device was sent me from a nun,
lovers-complaint-l233: Or sister sanctified, of holiest note;
lovers-complaint-l234: Which late her noble suit in court did shun,
lovers-complaint-l235: Whose rarest havings made the blossoms dote;
lovers-complaint-l236: For she was sought by spirits of richest coat,
lovers-complaint-l237: But kept cold distance, and did thence remove,
lovers-complaint-l238: To spend her living in eternal love.
lovers-complaint-l239: “ ‘But, O my sweet, what labour is’t to leave
lovers-complaint-l240: The thing we have not, mastering what not strives,
lovers-complaint-l241: Playing the place which did no form receive,
lovers-complaint-l242: Playing patient sports in unconstrained gyves?
lovers-complaint-l243: She that her fame so to herself contrives,
lovers-complaint-l244: The scars of battle ’scapeth by the flight,
lovers-complaint-l245: And makes her absence valiant, not her might.
lovers-complaint-l246: “ ‘O, pardon me, in that my boast is true:
lovers-complaint-l247: The accident which brought me to her eye
lovers-complaint-l248: Upon the moment did her force subdue,
lovers-complaint-l249: And now she would the caged cloister fly:
lovers-complaint-l250: Religious love put out Religion’s eye:
lovers-complaint-l251: Not to be tempted, would she be immured,
lovers-complaint-l252: And now, to tempt, all liberty procured.
lovers-complaint-l253: “ ‘How mighty then you are, O, hear me tell!
lovers-complaint-l254: The broken bosoms that to me belong
lovers-complaint-l255: Have emptied all their fountains in my well,
lovers-complaint-l256: And mine I pour your ocean all among:
lovers-complaint-l257: I strong o’er them, and you o’er me being strong,
lovers-complaint-l258: Must for your victory us all congest,
lovers-complaint-l259: As compound love to physic your cold breast.
lovers-complaint-l260: “ ‘My parts had power to charm a sacred nun,
lovers-complaint-l261: Who, disciplined, ay, dieted in grace,
lovers-complaint-l262: Believed her eyes when they to assail begun,
lovers-complaint-l263: All vows and consecrations giving place:
lovers-complaint-l264: O most potential love! vow, bond, nor space,
lovers-complaint-l265: In thee hath neither sting, knot, nor confine,
lovers-complaint-l266: For thou art all, and all things else are thine.
lovers-complaint-l267: “ ‘When thou impressest, what are precepts worth
lovers-complaint-l268: Of stale example? When thou wilt inflame,
lovers-complaint-l269: How coldly those impediments stand forth
lovers-complaint-l270: Of wealth, of filial fear, law, kindred, fame!
lovers-complaint-l271: Love’s arms are peace, ’gainst rule, ’gainst sense, ’gainst shame,
lovers-complaint-l272: And sweetens, in the suffering pangs it bears,
lovers-complaint-l273: The aloes of all forces, shocks, and fears.
lovers-complaint-l274: “ ‘Now all these hearts that do on mine depend,
lovers-complaint-l275: Feeling it break, with bleeding groans they pine;
lovers-complaint-l276: And supplicant their sighs to your extend,
lovers-complaint-l277: To leave the battery that you make ’gainst mine,
lovers-complaint-l278: Lending soft audience to my sweet design,
lovers-complaint-l279: And credent soul to that strong-bonded oath
lovers-complaint-l280: That shall prefer and undertake my troth.’
lovers-complaint-l281: “This said, his watery eyes he did dismount,
lovers-complaint-l282: Whose sights till then were levell’d on my face;
lovers-complaint-l283: Each cheek a river running from a fount
lovers-complaint-l284: With brinish current downward flow’d apace:
lovers-complaint-l285: O, how the channel to the stream gave grace!
lovers-complaint-l286: Who glazed with crystal gate the glowing roses
lovers-complaint-l287: That flame through water which their hue encloses.
lovers-complaint-l288: “O father, what a hell of witchcraft lies
lovers-complaint-l289: In the small orb of one particular tear!
lovers-complaint-l290: But with the inundation of the eyes
lovers-complaint-l291: What rocky heart to water will not wear?
lovers-complaint-l292: What breast so cold that is not warmed here?
lovers-complaint-l293: O cleft effect! cold modesty, hot wrath,
lovers-complaint-l294: Both fire from hence and chill extincture hath.
lovers-complaint-l295: “For, lo, his passion, but an art of craft,
lovers-complaint-l296: Even there resolved my reason into tears;
lovers-complaint-l297: There my white stole of chastity I daff’d,
lovers-complaint-l298: Shook off my sober guards and civil fears;
lovers-complaint-l299: Appear to him, as he to me appears,
lovers-complaint-l300: All melting; though our drops this difference bore,
lovers-complaint-l301: His poison’d me, and mine did him restore.
lovers-complaint-l302: “In him a plenitude of subtle matter,
lovers-complaint-l303: Applied to cautels, all strange forms receives,
lovers-complaint-l304: Of burning blushes, or of weeping water,
lovers-complaint-l305: Or swooning paleness; and he takes and leaves,
lovers-complaint-l306: In either’s aptness, as it best deceives,
lovers-complaint-l307: To blush at speeches rank, to weep at woes,
lovers-complaint-l308: Or to turn white and swoon at tragic shows:
lovers-complaint-l309: “That not a heart which in his level came
lovers-complaint-l310: Could ’scape the hail of his all-hurting aim,
lovers-complaint-l311: Showing fair nature is both kind and tame;
lovers-complaint-l312: And, veil’d in them, did win whom he would maim:
lovers-complaint-l313: Against the thing he sought he would exclaim;
lovers-complaint-l314: When he most burn’d in heart-wish’d luxury,
lovers-complaint-l315: He preach’d pure maid, and praised cold chastity.
lovers-complaint-l316: “Thus merely with the garment of a Grace
lovers-complaint-l317: The naked and concealed fiend he cover’d;
lovers-complaint-l318: That th’ unexperient gave the tempter place,
lovers-complaint-l319: Which like a cherubin above them hover’d.
lovers-complaint-l320: Who, young and simple, would not be so lover’d?
lovers-complaint-l321: Ay me! I fell; and yet do question make
lovers-complaint-l322: What I should do again for such a sake.
lovers-complaint-l323: “O, that infected moisture of his eye,
lovers-complaint-l324: O, that false fire which in his cheek so glow’d,
lovers-complaint-l325: O, that forced thunder from his heart did fly,
lovers-complaint-l326: O, that sad breath his spongy lungs bestow’d,
lovers-complaint-l327: O, all that borrow’d motion seeming owed,
lovers-complaint-l328: Would yet again betray the fore-betray’d,
lovers-complaint-l329: And new pervert a reconciled maid!”
